title: Weak naive fibrations to naive fibrant presheaves lift against monomorphisms
statement:
Fix an input universe as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a small ordinary category and $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(A^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Set})$. Let $1$ be its terminal presheaf and $I$ a presheaf with maps $e_0,e_1:1\to I$ such that $\delta=(e_0,e_1):1\amalg1\to I$ is monic. For $i:U\to V$ and $j:K\to L$, put $i\square j:(V\times K)\amalg_{U\times K}(U\times L)\to V\times L$. Let $\mathrm{An}$ be the closure of a small set of monomorphisms under isomorphisms, pushouts, small transfinite compositions and arrow retracts. Assume $e_\varepsilon\square j\in\mathrm{An}$ for every monomorphism $j$ and $\varepsilon=0,1$, and $\delta\square i\in\mathrm{An}$ for every $i\in\mathrm{An}$. A map has the right lifting property against a class if every commutative square with left side in that class has a diagonal filler. Call a map naive fibrant if it has the right lifting property against $\mathrm{An}$, and an object $Z$ naive fibrant if $Z\to1$ is such a map. Write $[K,Z]_I$ for maps $K\to Z$ modulo the equivalence relation generated by the endpoint restrictions of maps $K\times I\to Z$. Let $W_I$ be the maps $u:K\to L$ for which $[L,Z]_I\to[K,Z]_I$ is bijective for every naive fibrant $Z$ in the input universe.

If $p:X\to Y$ is a naive fibrant map and $Y$ is naive fibrant, then $p\in W_I$ if and only if $p$ has the right lifting property against every monomorphism of presheaves. No model structure is assumed.

source.place: Cisinski, Higher Categories and Homotopical Algebra, Lemma 2.4.28, using Lemmas 2.4.24 and 2.4.27; printed pp. 58-61 (PDF pp. 73-76). Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this interval-homotopy lemma.

proof.text: Write $0,1$ for the two endpoint sections, and write homotopies with domain $I\times T$ using the symmetry of products. All formulas below are componentwise formulas compatible with presheaf restrictions. Since $\delta$ is monic, the endpoints are disjoint subpresheaves and $\partial I\times T=(\{0\}\times T)\amalg(\{1\}\times T)\hookrightarrow I\times T$ is monic. The domains of the pushout products used below are the indicated unions: objectwise the pushout identifies just the intersection of its two subsets. Maps agreeing on that intersection therefore glue to a natural presheaf map.

source.place: Example 2.4.10 and Remark 2.4.9; product-cylinder and union conventions, checked objectwise.

proof.text: Let $Z$ be naive fibrant and let $a,b,c:T\to Z$ have direct homotopies $h:a\sim b$ and $k:a\sim c$. On $I_r\times\{0\}\times T$ prescribe $h(r,-)$, on $I_r\times\{1\}\times T$ prescribe $k(r,-)$, and on $\{0\}\times I_t\times T$ prescribe $a$. These agree on both intersections. The union inclusion into $I_r\times I_t\times T$ is $e_0\square(\delta\times T)$, hence belongs to $\mathrm{An}$ by the first interval axiom, since $\delta\times T$ is monic. A lift into $Z$ exists by its naive fibrancy. Restriction to $r=1$ has endpoints $b,c$.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.24, printed pp. 58-59 (PDF pp. 73-74); the three-face filler written explicitly.

proof.text: A constant homotopy gives reflexivity. In Step 2 take $c=a$ and $k$ constant to obtain symmetry. If $a\sim b\sim c$, symmetry gives $b\sim a$ and Step 2 applied to $b\sim a,b\sim c$ gives $a\sim c$. Thus for a naive fibrant target the direct relation is already an equivalence relation, so equality in $[T,Z]_I$ is witnessed by one direct homotopy in either specified orientation. Also, precomposition of $H:I\times T\to Z$ with $1_I\times v$ and postcomposition with any $w:Z\to Z'$ show directly that both operations descend to the generated homotopy quotients.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.24 and Definition 2.4.14; symmetry, transitivity and composition of homotopy classes expanded.

proof.text: The object $X$ is naive fibrant. Indeed, for $i:U\to V$ in $\mathrm{An}$ and $a:U\to X$, extend $pa$ to $b:V\to Y$ using naive fibrancy of $Y$. Lift the square $(a,b)$ against $i$ and $p$. Its diagonal extends $a$ to $V$, proving the terminal-map lifting property for $X$.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.28, first sentence; source fibrancy hypothesis verified directly by two successive lifts.

proof.text: Assume $p\in W_I$. Since $X$ is an allowed naive fibrant test by Step 4, surjectivity of $p^*:[Y,X]_I\to[X,X]_I$ supplies a representative $t:Y\to X$ with $[tp]=[1_X]$. Postcomposing this equality with $p$ gives $[ptp]=[p]$.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.26; the required homotopy-Yoneda surjectivity calculation written out instead of invoked.

proof.text: Since $Y$ is an allowed naive fibrant test, $p^*:[Y,Y]_I\to[X,Y]_I$ is injective. The equality in Step 5 is $p^*([pt])=p^*([1_Y])$, so $[pt]=[1_Y]$. Step 3 now gives a direct homotopy $k:I\times Y\to Y$ with $k(0,-)=1_Y$ and $k(1,-)=pt$.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.26 and the first part of Lemma 2.4.28; injectivity calculation and actual homotopy specified.

proof.text: The map $e_1\times Y:Y\hookrightarrow I\times Y$ is $e_1\square(\varnothing\hookrightarrow Y)$ and belongs to $\mathrm{An}$. The square with this left map, top $t:Y\to X$, bottom $k:I\times Y\to Y$, and right $p$ commutes because $k(1,-)=pt$. Lift it to $k':I\times Y\to X$ and put $s=k'(0,-)$. Then $ps=k(0,-)=1_Y$, while $k'(1,-)=t$.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.28, printed p. 60 (PDF p. 75); correction of the homotopy inverse to a strict section.

proof.text: The homotopy $k'$ gives $[s]=[t]$, and precomposition with $p$ gives $[sp]=[tp]=[1_X]$. By Steps 3 and 4 choose an actual homotopy $h:I\times X\to X$ with $h(0,-)=1_X$ and $h(1,-)=sp$. At this stage no equation $ph=p\operatorname{pr}_X$ has been assumed.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.28, printed p. 60; deriving the second homotopy from the lifted section.

proof.text: In $I_r\times I_t\times X$ let $D=(\{1\}\times I_t\times X)\cup(I_r\times\partial I_t\times X)$. Prescribe $sp(x)$ on $r=1$, $h(r,x)$ on $t=0$, and $sp(h(r,x))$ on $t=1$. These glue: at $(r,t)=(1,0)$ both values are $sp(x)$; at $(1,1)$ use $spsp=sp$, which follows from $ps=1_Y$. Their composites with $p$ equal the restriction of $b(r,t,x)=ph(r,x)$: on $t=1$ use $ps=1_Y$, and on $r=1$ use $ph(1,x)=psp(x)=p(x)$.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.28, final square, printed pp. 60-61 (PDF pp. 75-76); all face and base compatibilities written explicitly.

proof.text: The inclusion $D\hookrightarrow I_r\times I_t\times X$ is $e_1\square(\delta\times X)$, in $\mathrm{An}$ since $\delta\times X$ is monic. Lift the commutative square of Step 9 against $p$, obtaining $H$ with $pH=b$. Set $K(t,x)=H(0,t,x)$. Its endpoints are $K(0,x)=h(0,x)=x$ and $K(1,x)=sp(h(0,x))=sp(x)$, and $pK(t,x)=ph(0,x)=p(x)$. Thus $K$ is the required homotopy over $Y$, from $1_X$ to $sp$.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.28, final square and endpoint identities, printed p. 61 (PDF p. 76).

proof.text: Let $i:U\hookrightarrow V$ be any monomorphism and let $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$ satisfy $pa=bi$. On $(I\times U)\cup(\{1\}\times V)$ prescribe $K(t,a(u))$ on the first part and $sb(v)$ on the second. They agree on the intersection since $K(1,a(u))=spa(u)=sbi(u)$. Their images under $p$ agree with $b\operatorname{pr}_V$, since $pK(t,a(u))=pa(u)=bi(u)$ and $psb=b$. The union inclusion into $I\times V$ is $e_1\square i\in\mathrm{An}$.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.27, printed pp. 59-60 (PDF pp. 74-75); the arbitrary monomorphism square and its prescribed homotopy.

proof.text: Lift the square of Step 11 against $p$ to $L:I\times V\to X$. The map $l(v)=L(0,v)$ satisfies $li(u)=K(0,a(u))=a(u)$ and $pl(v)=b(v)$. Since the original monomorphism square was arbitrary, $p$ has the right lifting property against every monomorphism. This proves the forward implication.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.27, final two equations; completion of the forward implication of Lemma 2.4.28.

proof.text: Conversely assume $p$ lifts against every monomorphism. Lifting the square with left map $\varnothing\hookrightarrow Y$, bottom $1_Y$ and right $p$ supplies $s:Y\to X$ with $ps=1_Y$. The map $\delta\times X:X\amalg X\hookrightarrow I\times X$ is monic. Prescribe $(1_X,sp)$ on its endpoints and $p\operatorname{pr}_X:I\times X\to Y$ on the bottom; the square commutes because $psp=p$. Its lift is a direct homotopy $Q:1_X\sim sp$.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.17, printed p. 56 (PDF p. 71); the two elementary lifts needed for the converse.

proof.text: For any allowed naive fibrant $Z$, precomposition with $s$ defines an inverse to $p^*:[Y,Z]_I\to[X,Z]_I$. On a representative $f:Y\to Z$, one composite gives $fps=f$. On $g:X\to Z$, the other gives $gsp$, homotopic to $g$ by $gQ$. Step 3 ensures the operations are well defined on the quotients. Thus every testing map is bijective and $p\in W_I$, proving the converse. All tests $X,Y$ and all finite products, unions and chosen maps above remain in the given input universe.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.17 and Remark 2.4.21; explicit inverse functions on homotopy quotients, as used for the converse of Lemma 2.4.28.
